clue.text: Opportunity to get fish — one paid at this gate

parts.note: your turn is your opportunity to act
the pike is a predatory freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler gets the chance of a catch, and someone has to be paid at the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a turnpike was a gate across a road where a toll was paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a toll gate barring a road, where travellers paid a fee to pass.

clue.text: The unending stream that brings excitement

indicators.note: unending means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A never-ending river brings a sense of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a sudden wave of pleasurable excitement or a buzz.

clue.text: Rangers? Some other football team!

definitions.meaning: many clubs take this name, such as Blackburn or Bristol

explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is a Scottish football club; the answer names other clubs, such as Blackburn Rovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: wanderers who roam about, and a common British football club name.

clue.text: Dad has charge as befits one in his position

definitions.text: as befits one in his position

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for dad
a rental is a charge for hire

explanation.surface: A father takes charge in a way that suits his role.
explanation.definitionFit: A father's position is that of mother or father, so what suits it is fatherly or motherly.

clue.text: Characters from Stoke, energetic and enthusiastic

indicators.note: Characters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fans from Stoke are lively and eager.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'and', which is only a link; the definition is 'enthusiastic'. Stoke is a city in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: eager or keen people are full of enthusiasm.

clue.text: A maiden locked in hut, disgraced

indicators.note: something locked in a building is enclosed by it, so these letters go inside the hut word

parts.note: a shed is a simple hut
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman shut in a hut has been brought into disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to be disgraced is to be put to shame publicly.

clue.text: Cut is harsh, one admitted, having nothing

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the one goes inside the harsh word

parts.note: hard means harsh
I is the Roman numeral one
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A severe haircut, with one person allowed in for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb but is a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A haircut or styled arrangement of hair is called this informally.

clue.text: Take action when silly gran gets stuck in shrub

indicators.note: gets stuck in means these letters are lodged inside the action word

parts.note: to move is to take action

indicators.note: silly signals the letters of gran are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone must act when a foolish grandmother is caught in a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take action' reads as an instruction but is the outer verb; 'silly' jumbles gran to ANGR before it 'gets stuck in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tree or shrub growing in coastal swamps with tangled roots.

clue.text: 'Morse' may be intelligible to such folk

definitions.text: 'Morse' may be intelligible to such folk

parts.words: 'Morse' may be intelligible to such folk
parts.note: Morse code makes sense to people who translate signals

explanation.walkthrough: Morse suggests the TV detective, but means Morse code, which these people translate.
explanation.definitionFit: People who turn coded signals back into plain language are translators of cipher.

clue.text: What has flower going over it?

definitions.text: What has flower going over it?

parts.words: What has flower going over it?
parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, a river, which runs over its bed

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'flower' as flow-er, a thing that flows: a river runs over its bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The channel floor along which a stream's water runs is exactly what that flowing thing passes over.

clue.text: Copper going about in charge of part of UK — easy task?

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it, so the policeman's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: PC, police constable, is a copper
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A policeman on patrol in charge of a region of the UK might find it a soft job.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something easy is said to be no outing in the park, a doddle.

clue.text: Old female set up to rule in another country

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: to reign is to rule

explanation.surface: An elderly woman is elevated to rule a land abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alien or overseas belongs to or happens in a nation other than your own.

clue.text: Zoologist learning somewhere down under

parts.note: lore is accumulated learning or knowledge
NZ, New Zealand, is a country 'down under' in the southern hemisphere

explanation.surface: A zoologist picks up knowledge somewhere in Australasia.
explanation.walkthrough: Konrad Lorenz was the Austrian zoologist famous for studying imprinting in geese.
explanation.definitionFit: Konrad Lorenz, Nobel-winning Austrian ethologist, is an example of this scientist.

clue.text: Gained by act with little right in it and felt doubt

parts.note: won means gained

indicators.note: in it means the small letter goes inside the act word just named

parts.note: a deed is an act
R is the short form of right

explanation.surface: Someone won through a deed with a scrap of justice in it, yet still had doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to have wondered whether something was so is to have felt doubt about it.

clue.text: Fair play, only with cold formality?

parts.note: just means only
ice is cold reserve or formality of manner

explanation.surface: Is fair dealing merely a matter of chilly protocol?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: fairness and equitable treatment of everyone.

clue.text: Greets special soldiers with musical instrument's introduction

indicators.note: introduction here means putting something in, so the instrument is placed inside the soldiers' letters

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service regiment
the lute is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Special forces are welcomed with a fanfare struck up on an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduction' looks like a first letter, but here it means inserting the instrument into the regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone who salutes another person greets them, often formally.

clue.text: Series of deliveries at an end

definitions.meaning: in cricket six balls bowled in sequence by one bowler form this unit

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a cricket set of six balls, and the adjective for finished or concluded.

clue.text: Acquire grip?

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to buy something, and a firm hold or foothold giving leverage.

clue.text: See servant tear about, almost doing nothing afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards places the second piece after the first
about signals the letters of tear are rearranged
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: inert means inactive, doing nothing

explanation.surface: Look at the servant rushing about, then barely doing anything afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' rearranges TEAR to RETA; 'almost' trims INERT to INER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a retainer is a long-serving household attendant.

clue.text: Target landing in grass, being shot down

indicators.note: landing in means the target word ends up inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a butt is a target, as in the butt of a joke

explanation.surface: A target falls into the grass after being shot down.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an argument that has been shot down has been refuted.

clue.text: American journalist may be exhausted

parts.note: ED, editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: An American reporter might well be worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: supplies that are exhausted have been consumed entirely.

clue.text: Surprise when celebrity is found to have carried bomb around

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so the celebrity's letters enclose the bomb

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: around signals the bomb word turned back to front

parts.note: egg is old RAF slang for a bomb

explanation.surface: It is a shock when a famous person turns out to have been carrying a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg was RAF slang for a bomb in the Second World War; 'around' turns it to GGE before the star carries it.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonyms: to astonish or astound someone, leaving them reeling.

clue.text: Light yellow bog with loose content

indicators.note: content here means contents, so the loose word fills the bog word

parts.note: a fen is a bog or marsh
lax means loose

explanation.surface: A pale yellow marsh with slack water in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like satisfied, but means the contents placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair the colour of flax fibre is pale blond, so a light yellow shade.

clue.text: Test is dull — minimal scoring!

parts.note: dry means dull
a single run is the smallest score in cricket

explanation.surface: A dreary cricket test with hardly any runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or trial before the real thing is called this idiom.

clue.text: Sort of road through defile

parts.note: by means through or via
a defile is a narrow mountain pass

explanation.surface: A kind of road that runs through a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defile' looks like a verb meaning sully, but is a narrow pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road diverting traffic around a town centre is an example of this.

clue.text: Woman who does hair — a wild weedy type!

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner who 'does' for a household
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: A cleaner who also styles hair is a bit of a wild one.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is British for a woman hired to clean someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlock is wild mustard, a common yellow-flowered weed of fields.

clue.text: Animal hunted in excavated area

definitions.meaning: a pit where stone is dug out

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the creature a hunter pursues, and an open pit where stone is extracted.

clue.text: It's dry nevertheless above and below river

indicators.note: in a down clue the word splits to sit above and below the river letter, enclosing it

parts.note: but means nevertheless

explanation.surface: Even so, it stays dry upstream and downstream of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut describes the driest style of champagne or sparkling wine.

clue.text: Girl by river building that's been added on

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
the Exe is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A girl beside the river stands by an extension to the house.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension or wing joined to a main building is called by this name.

clue.text: African city airport given makeover, full of energy

indicators.note: full of means the rearranged letters hold the energy letter inside
a makeover changes something's look, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An airport has been refurbished and is buzzing with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given makeover' turns AIRPORT into PRTORIA, and 'full of' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is South Africa's administrative capital, an example of a city there.

clue.text: Make a mistake and trip

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone slips up and then stumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' looks like a stumble, but it means a short journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a short journey taken to do a task, such as fetching shopping.

clue.text: Learners in hospital department restricted by bosses

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being held within it, so the department sits inside

parts.note: studs are bosses, raised knobs on a surface
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Trainees in a hospital department are kept in check by their superiors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bosses' suggests managers, but here it means knobs or studs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: people learning at college or school are pupils of their subject.
